rendering.persona_description: Nour is a 24-year-old transgender woman who works part-time at a plant nursery and takes evening classes toward a horticulture certificate. She likes identifying plants on walks, listening to true crime podcasts (though she's tried to cut back since they make her anxious), and going to a weekly D&D game with friends. She's been on hormone therapy for about a year and a half and is generally happy with how things are going for her transition, apart from the anxiety.
rendering.clinical_context: Nour has illness anxiety centered on cardiac and neurological sensations; she'll notice a skipped heartbeat, a tingling hand, or a headache and spiral into fear that it signals something serious like a heart condition or a tumor. It started about two years ago after a coworker was hospitalized suddenly, and got worse for a while when she began hormone therapy and started noticing new, unfamiliar body sensations she didn't have a frame of reference for. She's never gotten treatment for it, though she's thought about looking into therapy a few times and manages day to day by trying (not always successfully) not to check her pulse or look up symptoms.
rendering.behavioral_description: Nour is polite and a little apologetic in how she talks, often prefacing things with 'this is probably nothing but.' She goes along easily with whatever is suggested to her and says things like 'yeah, that makes sense' even when she isn't sure she'll actually do it. She tends to describe symptoms in detail and then quickly ask if that sounds normal or if she should be worried, and she'll agree to a plan out loud while still holding onto the anxious thought underneath.

traits.living_situation: lives with a roommate in a shared apartment
traits.help_seeking_orientation: open to suggestions in the moment but hasn't followed through on getting treatment, and prone to reassurance-seeking instead
traits.cognitive_style: catastrophizing about bodily sensations, ruminative, quick to seek reassurance

clinical_history.presentation: illness anxiety (illness anxiety disorder) focused on cardiac and neurological sensations
clinical_history.history: Onset roughly two years ago following a coworker's sudden hospitalization; worsened for a period after starting hormone therapy when new bodily sensations felt unfamiliar and alarming. She has never started a course of treatment for it, though she's considered looking into therapy a few times.
